goal: must fix core Agent resolution so plugin command calls such as ctx.agent.call(prompt, { commandId: "workflow.publish" }) resolve through the normal default/profile fallback policy when no plugin-specific override exists.

analysis.problem: Plugin commands receive the core Agent instance through the plugin context, but Agent.resolve(commandId) can return null for plugin command ids that are not mapped in the active profile. In the observed project config, agent.default is "codex" and agent.useProfile is "codex-only"; workflow.publish is not present in that profile, so publish failed with a generic "No agent configured" error even though default agent settings existed.
analysis.proposedApproach: Keep plugin-specific provider/profile overrides first, then make core Agent resolution apply the same fallback policy for plugin command ids as normal command ids: active profile prefix, default profile prefix, generic default provider key, and clear diagnostics when none resolves.
analysis.validation: Existing code shows createPluginAgentApi forwards dotted plugin command ids to agent.call, Agent.resolve delegates profile/default selection to resolveProfileKey, and ProviderRegistry can resolve provider-family keys such as "codex" by falling back to a built-in profile prefix. Existing docs describe agent.default as a provider key, so the fix targets resolution consistency and diagnostics rather than adding plugin-specific configuration requirements.

qa.question: Goal confirmation: must this spec fix the core Agent fallback so plugin command ids such as workflow.publish resolve without requiring each plugin command id to be present in the active profile?
qa.answer: must fix core Agent fallback for plugin command ids so workflow.publish and other plugin operations do not require explicit active-profile mappings when a generic default can resolve.
qa.evidence: Issue #378 Expected fix requires generic default agent resolution for ctx.agent.call(prompt, { commandId: "<plugin>.<operation>" }); src/lib/agent.js createPluginAgentApi forwards dotted command ids unchanged to agent.call.

qa.question: agent.default policy: should a provider-family default such as "codex" be treated as a resolvable generic provider key when ProviderRegistry has a built-in codex profile, instead of requiring a full key such as "codex/gpt-5.4"?
qa.answer: should keep provider-family defaults such as "codex" resolvable when ProviderRegistry can resolve that provider family; unresolvable values must fail with clearer diagnostics.

qa.considered: Requiring a full key such as codex/gpt-5.4 was considered, but it would leave the observed default unusable despite existing registry semantics.
